source.primary_witnesses: MT BHS Codex Leningradensis — entirely Hebrew. **THE RESURRECTION CHAPTER** — the most explicit canonical HB statement of two-fold bodily resurrection. SECONDARY: 4Q114 (Danielc) preserves portions of ch 12. The Qumran witness confirms the MT outline; 4Q174 (Florilegium) and 11Q13 (Melchizedek) demonstrate the Daniel-eschatology was foundational for Qumran sectarian thought. TERTIARY: OG-Greek + Theodotion-Greek consulted at the calendrical figures (vv 7, 11, 12). The OG of ch 12 is one of the better-preserved sections; minor variants at v 13.
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against BHS apparatus + DJD XVI 2000 + Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.fetchedFrom: BHS; Ulrich DJD XVI 2000; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999.
source.citation: BHS (Deutsche Bibelgesellschaft 1997); Ulrich et al. 2000 DJD XVI; Collins 1993 Hermeneia; Goldingay 1989 WBC; Newsom 2014 OTL; Montgomery 1927 ICC; Ziegler-Munnich 1999 Septuaginta XVI.2.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 12 — HEBREW, the final chapter. **MAJOR ESCHATOLOGICAL CONTENT**: (1) Michael's eschatological intervention (v 1); (2) the **TWO-FOLD RESURRECTION** (v 2) — foundational HB resurrection text, with *ḥayyê ʿōlām* (everlasting life) vs *dirʾôn ʿōlām* (everlasting contempt); (3) the wise shining like stars (v 3); (4) the sealed book (vv 4, 9); (5) the three apocalyptic calendar-numbers: time/times/half (v 7), 1290 days (v 11), 1335 days (v 12). The chapter is the densest single concentration of cross-corpus-influential eschatology in the HB. **CROSS-CORPUS DENSITY**: Isa 26:19 (resurrection); 2 Macc 7 (martyrs' resurrection); Mk 12:25; Jn 11:25; 1 Thess 4:16; Rev 20:12-15; 1 En 22, 90:33; 2 Bar 30; 4 Ezra 7.

verses.text: וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִיא֩ יַעֲמֹ֨ד מִֽיכָאֵ֜ל הַשַּׂ֣ר הַגָּד֗וֹל הָעֹמֵד֮ עַל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּךָ֒ וְהָיְתָה֙ עֵ֣ת צָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נִהְיְתָה֙ מִֽהְי֣וֹת גּ֔וֹי עַ֖ד הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט עַמְּךָ֔ כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בַּסֵּֽפֶר׃
verses.translit: ū-ḇā-ʿēṯ ha-hîʾ yaʿămōḏ Mîḵāʾēl haś-śar hag-gāḏōl hā-ʿōmēḏ ʿal-bənê ʿammeḵā wə-hāyəṯāh ʿēṯ ṣārāh ʾăšer lōʾ-nihyəṯāh mi-hyōṯ gōy ʿaḏ hā-ʿēṯ ha-hîʾ ū-ḇā-ʿēṯ ha-hîʾ yim-mālēṭ ʿammə-ḵā kol-han-nimṣāʾ kāṯūḇ bas-sēp̄er
verses.notes: **'At that time shall arise Michael, the great prince who has charge of your people. And there shall be a time of trouble, such as never has been since there was a nation till that time. But at that time your people shall be delivered, every one whose name shall be found written in the book.'** **MICHAEL AS ISRAEL'S PRINCE** — cf. 10:13, 10:21. **'GREAT PRINCE'** (הַשַּׂר הַגָּדוֹל haś-śar hag-gāḏōl). **'TIME OF TROUBLE UNPARALLELED'**: the tribulation-trope. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR NT**: (a) Matt 24:21 + Mark 13:19: 'there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world... no, and never will be' — DIRECT Dan 12:1 quotation in Jesus's Olivet discourse. (b) Rev 12:7-9: 'Michael and his angels fought against the dragon' — Michael's eschatological role. (c) Jude 9 (Michael disputing with Satan). **'BOOK'** — the book of life. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Exod 32:32-33; Ps 69:28; Mal 3:16; cf. Luke 10:20; Phil 4:3; Rev 3:5, 13:8, 17:8, 20:12, 20:15, 21:27 ('book of life of the Lamb'). Cross-corpus to 12:1 Michael as Israel's prince-angel + Rev 12:7 + Jude 9.

verses.text: וְרַבִּ֕ים מִיְּשֵׁנֵ֥י אַדְמַת־עָפָ֖ר יָקִ֑יצוּ אֵ֚לֶּה לְחַיֵּ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם וְאֵ֥לֶּה לַחֲרָפ֖וֹת לְדִרְא֥וֹן עוֹלָֽם׃
verses.translit: wə-rabbîm miy-yəšēnê ʾaḏmaṯ-ʿāp̄ār yāqîṣū ʾēlleh lə-ḥayyê ʿōlām wə-ʾēlleh la-ḥărāp̄ōṯ lə-ḏirʾōn ʿōlām
verses.notes: **'And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.'** **THE FOUNDATIONAL HB RESURRECTION TEXT** — the only unambiguous canonical-HB statement of bodily resurrection of individuals to differentiated eternal destinies. **KEY TERMS**: (a) יְשֵׁנֵי אַדְמַת־עָפָר (yəšēnê ʾaḏmaṯ-ʿāp̄ār 'those sleeping in the dust of the earth') — 'sleep' as euphemism for death. (b) חַיֵּי עוֹלָם (ḥayyê ʿōlām 'everlasting life') — the only HB occurrence; foundational for rabbinic *ḥayyê ʿōlām hab-bāʾ* ('life of the world-to-come') and Christian *zōē aiōnios* ('eternal life'). (c) דִּרְאוֹן עוֹלָם (dirʾōn ʿōlām 'everlasting contempt/abhorrence') — root *drʾ* ('repulse'); cf. Isa 66:24 ('they shall be an abhorrence — דֵרָאוֹן dērāʾōn — to all flesh') — Daniel quotes Isaiah's verse on the final destiny of the wicked. **'MANY' (רַבִּים rabbîm)**: scholarly debate — does this mean (a) the *limited* resurrection of the maskilim + the apostates only (Collins's reading: not all-humanity); (b) general resurrection (rabbinic + Christian reading)? **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: (i) **Isa 26:19**: 'your dead shall live, their bodies shall rise. O dwellers in the dust, awake and sing for joy!' — earlier proto-resurrection text; Daniel is the canonical fulfillment. (ii) **2 Macc 7** (the martyrdom of the seven brothers + mother): explicit two-fold resurrection-faith of the Maccabean martyrs (vv 9, 11, 14, 23, 29, 36) — contemporary with Daniel and elaborates the same hope. (iii) **Wisdom 3:1-9** (souls of the righteous in God's hand). (iv) **Mark 12:25 / Matt 22:30 / Luke 20:36**: Jesus on resurrection ('they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels'). (v) **John 5:28-29**: 'all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out — those who have done good, to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment' — direct Dan 12:2 two-fold-resurrection inheritance. (vi) **John 11:25**: 'I am the resurrection and the life.' (vii) **1 Thess 4:16**: 'the dead in Christ will rise first.' (viii) **1 Cor 15** (resurrection chapter). (ix) **Rev 20:5-6, 20:12-15** (the great-white-throne judgment + the book of life vs the lake of fire). (x) **1 En 22**: the four chambers of Sheol holding souls awaiting judgment. (xi) **2 Bar 30** + **4 Ezra 7**: post-70-CE Jewish resurrection-theologies. (xii) **m. Sanhedrin 10:1**: 'all Israel has a share in the world-to-come' — except those who deny resurrection-from-the-dead-from-Torah (the rabbinic reading of Dan 12:2 + Isa 26:19 as Torah-canonical resurrection-proof-texts). Cross-corpus to 12:1-3 RESURRECTION + Isa 26:19 + 2 Macc 7 + Mark 12:25 + Jn 11:25 + 1 Thess 4:16 + Rev 20:12-15.

verses.text: וְהַ֨מַּשְׂכִּלִ֔ים יַזְהִ֖רוּ כְּזֹ֣הַר הָרָקִ֑יעַ וּמַצְדִּיקֵי֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים כַּכּוֹכָבִ֖ים לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃
verses.translit: wə-ham-maśkilîm yazhirū kə-zōhar hā-rāqîaʿ ū-maṣdîqê hā-rabbîm kak-kōḵāḇîm lə-ʿōlām wā-ʿeḏ
verses.notes: **'And those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament; and those who turn many to righteousness, like the stars for ever and ever.'** **THE GLORIFICATION OF THE MASKILIM**: the wise/insightful teachers (cf. 11:33, 11:35) receive astral glorification at resurrection. **KEY IMAGE**: כְּזֹהַר הָרָקִיעַ (kə-zōhar hā-rāqîaʿ 'like the brightness of the firmament') — note: זֹהַר zōhar is the namesake of the medieval Kabbalistic Zohar. **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: (a) **Matt 13:43**: 'then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father' — DIRECT Dan 12:3 quotation by Jesus, with 'sun' substituting for 'firmament/stars'. (b) **1 Cor 15:41-42**: 'There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars... so it is with the resurrection of the dead.' (c) **Phil 2:15**: 'shine as lights in the world'. (d) **1 En 104:2**: 'You shall shine like the lights of heaven, and the gate of heaven shall be opened to you' — direct Daniel inheritance. (e) **2 Bar 51:10**: the righteous made equal to angels and to stars. (f) **4Q521 (Messianic Apocalypse)** uses similar resurrection-glorification vocabulary. (g) **Wisdom 3:7**: 'in the time of their visitation they will shine forth.' The maskilim-as-stars-forever motif is one of the most enduring images of Jewish-Christian eschatology.

verses.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה דָֽנִיֵּ֗אל סְתֹ֧ם הַדְּבָרִ֛ים וַחֲתֹ֥ם הַסֵּ֖פֶר עַד־עֵ֣ת קֵ֑ץ יְשֹׁטְט֥וּ רַבִּ֖ים וְתִרְבֶּ֥ה הַדָּֽעַת׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾattāh Dāniyyēʾl səṯōm had-dəḇārîm wa-ḥăṯōm has-sēp̄er ʿaḏ-ʿēṯ qēṣ yəšōṭəṭū rabbîm wə-ṯirbeh had-dāʿaṯ
verses.notes: **'But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, until the time of the end. Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.'** **THE SEALED BOOK** (וַחֲתֹם הַסֵּפֶר wa-ḥăṯōm has-sēp̄er): apocalyptic-pseudonymity device — the book is presented as preserved for a far-future audience (the contemporaneous-with-text persecuted readers). **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: (a) **Rev 5:1-9**: 'a scroll written within and on the back, sealed with seven seals... and no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it... the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered, so that he can open the scroll' — Revelation's seven-sealed scroll is direct Dan 12:4 inheritance, with Christ as the worthy-one to open. (b) **Rev 22:10**: 'do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near' — Revelation REVERSES the Daniel seal-instruction, signaling that the apocalyptic-clock has now reached its terminus. (c) **Jub heavenly-tablets tradition** — analogous sealed-revelation. (d) Isa 29:11; Ezek 2:9-3:3 (the scroll given to eat). Cross-corpus to 12:4 + 12:9 SEALED BOOK until the time of the end + Rev 5:1 + Rev 22:10 + Jub heavenly tablets.

verses.text: וְרָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנַ֥יִם אֲחֵרִ֖ים עֹמְדִ֑ים אֶחָ֥ד הֵ֙נָּה֙ לִשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְאֹ֔ר וְאֶחָ֥ד הֵ֖נָּה לִשְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃
verses.translit: wə-rāʾîṯî ʾănî Dāniyyēʾl wə-hinnēh šənayim ʾăḥērîm ʿōmḏîm ʾeḥāḏ hēnnāh li-śp̄aṯ hay-yəʾōr wə-ʾeḥāḏ hēnnāh li-śp̄aṯ hay-yəʾōr
verses.notes: **Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others stood, one on this bank of the stream and one on that bank of the stream.** Two additional angels (besides the man-clothed-in-linen of v 6). The riverbank setting echoes 10:4 (the Tigris).

verses.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָאִישׁ֙ לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִמַּ֖עַל לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֑ר עַד־מָתַ֖י קֵ֥ץ הַפְּלָאֽוֹת׃
verses.translit: way-yōmer lā-ʾîš ləḇūš hab-baddîm ʾăšer mim-maʿal lə-mêmê hay-yəʾōr ʿaḏ-māṯay qēṣ hap-pəlāʾōṯ
verses.notes: **One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the stream: 'How long shall it be till the end of these wonders?'** **THE 'HOW LONG' QUESTION** — apocalyptic-trope. cf. 8:13; Zech 1:12; Rev 6:10 ('how long, O sovereign Lord'). The man-clothed-in-linen = the angelic figure of 10:5-6 — described identically.

verses.text: וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־הָאִ֣ישׁ ׀ לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִמַּעַל֮ לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹר֒ וַיָּ֨רֶם יְמִינ֤וֹ וּשְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע בְּחֵ֣י הָעוֹלָ֑ם כִּי֩ לְמוֹעֵ֨ד מֽוֹעֲדִ֜ים וָחֵ֗צִי וּכְכַלּ֛וֹת נַפֵּ֥ץ יַד־עַם־קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּכְלֶ֥ינָה כָל־אֵֽלֶּה׃
verses.translit: wā-ʾešmaʿ ʾeṯ-hā-ʾîš ləḇūš hab-baddîm ʾăšer mim-maʿal lə-mêmê hay-yəʾōr way-yārem yəmînō ū-śəmōʾlō ʾel-haš-šāmayim way-yiš-šāḇaʿ bə-ḥê hā-ʿōlām kî lə-mōʿēḏ mōʿăḏîm wā-ḥēṣî ū-ḵə-ḵallōṯ nappēṣ yaḏ-ʿam-qōḏeš tiḵleynāh ḵol-ʾēlleh
verses.notes: **The man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the stream, raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven; and I heard him swear by him who lives for ever that it would be for a time, two times, and half a time; and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things would be accomplished.** **THE TIME-TIMES-HALF-A-TIME FORMULA — IN HEBREW**: לְמוֹעֵד מוֹעֲדִים וָחֵצִי (lə-mōʿēḏ mōʿăḏîm wā-ḥēṣî). **DIRECT PARALLEL TO 7:25 ARAMAIC** (ʿiddān wə-ʿiddānîn ū-p̄əlaḡ ʿiddān). **CROSS-CORPUS — MAJOR**: appears as 'forty-two months' (Rev 11:2, 13:5); '1260 days' (Rev 11:3, 12:6); 'time, times, and half a time' (Rev 12:14) — these are the FOUR Revelation-equivalents of Dan 7:25 + 12:7's 3.5 years. **DOUBLE-HANDED OATH**: raising BOTH hands is the maximally-solemn oath-formula (a single hand suffices per Gen 14:22; Deut 32:40; the double-hand intensifies). **'BY HIM WHO LIVES FOR EVER'** (בְּחֵי הָעוֹלָם bə-ḥê hā-ʿōlām) — cf. Aramaic Dan 4:34 (ḥay ʿāləmāʾ); cf. Rev 10:5-6 (the angel of Rev 10 'raised his right hand to heaven and swore by him who lives for ever and ever' — DIRECT Dan 12:7 quotation). Cross-corpus to 12:7 + 12:11-12 calendar-arithmetic (1290 days + 1335 days).

verses.text: וַאֲנִ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה אֲדֹנִ֕י מָ֖ה אַחֲרִ֥ית אֵֽלֶּה׃
verses.translit: wa-ʾănî šāmaʿtî wə-lōʾ ʾāḇîn wā-ʾōmərāh ʾăḏōnî māh ʾaḥărîṯ ʾēlleh
verses.notes: **I heard, but I did not understand. Then I said: 'O my lord, what shall be the outcome of these things?'** **THE SEER'S UNCOMPREHENSION**: Daniel models the role of one who receives revelation without fully understanding it — the future-reader is required for interpretation.

verses.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֵ֣ךְ דָּנִיֵּ֑אל כִּֽי־סְתֻמִ֧ים וַחֲתֻמִ֛ים הַדְּבָרִ֖ים עַד־עֵ֥ת קֵֽץ׃
verses.translit: way-yōmer lēḵ Dāniyyēʾl kî-səṯumîm wa-ḥăṯumîm had-dəḇārîm ʿaḏ-ʿēṯ qēṣ
verses.notes: **He said: 'Go your way, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.'** Sealing-instruction repeated (cf. v 4). The closed-character-of-the-text is constitutive of its apocalyptic identity. Cross-corpus to 12:4 + 12:9 SEALED BOOK until the time of the end.

verses.text: יִ֠תְבָּֽרֲרוּ וְיִֽתְלַבְּנ֤וּ וְיִצָּֽרְפוּ֙ רַבִּ֔ים וְהִרְשִׁ֣יעוּ רְשָׁעִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָבִ֖ינוּ כָּל־רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהַמַּשְׂכִּלִ֖ים יָבִֽינוּ׃
verses.translit: yiṯ-bārărū wə-yiṯ-labbənū wə-yiṣ-ṣārəp̄ū rabbîm wə-hiršîʿū rəšāʿîm wə-lōʾ yāḇînū kol-rəšāʿîm wə-ham-maśkilîm yāḇînū
verses.notes: **'Many shall purify themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the wicked shall do wickedly; and none of the wicked shall understand; but those who are wise shall understand.'** **EPISTEMIC-DIVIDE THEME**: only the maskilim (the wise) understand the apocalyptic-vision; the wicked are outside the interpretive-community. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Matt 13:11-13 (the parables-teaching: 'to you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given'); cf. Rev 13:18 ('let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast'). The 'refining/whitening/purifying' triad echoes 11:35; cf. Mal 3:2-3.

verses.text: וּמֵעֵת֙ הוּסַ֣ר הַתָּמִ֔יד וְלָתֵ֖ת שִׁקּ֣וּץ שֹׁמֵ֑ם יָמִ֕ים אֶ֖לֶף מָאתַ֥יִם וְתִשְׁעִֽים׃
verses.translit: ū-mē-ʿēṯ hūsar hat-tāmîḏ wə-lā-ṯēṯ šiqqūṣ šōmēm yāmîm ʾelep̄ māʾṯayim wə-ṯišʿîm
verses.notes: **'And from the time that the continual burnt offering is taken away, and the abomination that makes desolate is set up, there shall be a thousand two hundred and ninety days.'** **THE 1290 DAYS** = approximately 3.5 lunar years + 1 intercalary month (3.5 × 360 = 1260; + 30 = 1290). **HISTORICAL FIT**: from the abolition of the *tāmîd* (December 167 BCE per 1 Macc 1:54) to the Temple rededication (25 Kislev 164 BCE per 1 Macc 4:52-54) ≈ 3 years + a few weeks — close to 1290 days but not exactly. The variant 1290 (v 11) vs 1335 (v 12) vs 1150 (8:14) vs 'time, times, and half' (7:25, 12:7) is the foundational Daniel calendar-arithmetic puzzle. Per Collins 1993, the variants may reflect successive recalculations during the persecution-period: as the predicted-end didn't arrive, the number was revised upward. **'ABOMINATION OF DESOLATION'** repeats from 11:31, 9:27. Cross-corpus to 12:7 + 12:11-12 calendar-arithmetic + 1290 days.

verses.text: אַשְׁרֵ֥י הַֽמְחַכֶּ֖ה וְיַגִּ֑יעַ לְיָמִ֕ים אֶ֕לֶף שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃
verses.translit: ʾašrê ham-ḥakkeh wə-yaggîaʿ lə-yāmîm ʾelep̄ šəlōš mēʾōṯ šəlōšîm wa-ḥămiššāh
verses.notes: **'Blessed is he who waits and comes to the thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.'** **THE 1335 DAYS**: 1290 + 45 days. The additional 45 days may signal: (a) a further extension as the predicted-end was delayed; (b) the period between the temple-rededication (164 BCE) and Antiochus IV's actual death (also 164 BCE) — beatitude for those who endured to see the persecutor's death. **'BLESSED'** (אַשְׁרֵי ʾašrê) — beatitude-form; cf. Ps 1:1; Matt 5:3-12. **CROSS-CORPUS**: cf. Rev 14:13 ('Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord'); Rev 20:6 ('Blessed and holy is the one who shares in the first resurrection'). Cross-corpus to 12:7 + 12:11-12 calendar-arithmetic + 1335 days.

verses.text: וְאַתָּ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ לַקֵּ֑ץ וְתָנ֛וּחַ וְתַעֲמֹ֥ד לְגֹרָלְךָ֖ לְקֵ֥ץ הַיָּמִֽין׃
verses.translit: wə-ʾattāh lēḵ laq-qēṣ wə-ṯānūaḥ wə-ṯaʿămōḏ lə-ḡōrāl-ḵā lə-qēṣ hay-yāmîn
verses.witness_tertiary: OG-Greek slightly variant; Theodotion closely follows MT
verses.notes: **'But go your way till the end; and you shall rest, and shall stand in your allotted place at the end of the days.'** **THE FINAL WORD TO DANIEL — INDIVIDUAL RESURRECTION PROMISE**: Daniel is told he will (a) 'rest' (תָנוּחַ ṯānūaḥ — die); (b) 'stand' (תַעֲמֹד taʿămōḏ — rise from the dead, in the technical resurrection-sense; cf. 12:2 yāqîṣū 'awake'); (c) receive his 'allotted place / portion' (גוֹרָל gōrāl — heritage in the world-to-come). **'END OF THE DAYS'** (קֵץ הַיָּמִין qēṣ hay-yāmîn) — note the unusual form *yāmîn* (not *yāmîm*); this may be a metathesis or a deliberate poetic variant. Some scholars read it as 'end of days at the right hand' (yāmîn 'right hand'), linking to Ps 110:1 messianic-typology. **CROSS-CORPUS**: (a) the verse is the foundational HB text for the individual-immortality + bodily-resurrection promise to the righteous. (b) cf. Wisdom 3:1-9 (souls of the righteous). (c) cf. Luke 23:43 ('today you will be with me in Paradise'). (d) cf. Rev 14:13 ('that they may rest from their labors'). (e) cf. m. Sanhedrin 10:1 (the rabbinic-resurrection-promise based on Dan 12:2, 12:13). **END OF THE BOOK OF DANIEL** — the Hebrew Bible's most explicit-eschatological prophet-text concludes with personal-resurrection-assurance to the seer himself, modeling for every reader the promise of individual share in the resurrection.
